title: Letters in the Wrong Envelopes
statement: A secretary puts $100$ letters into $100$ addressed envelopes completely at random, one letter per envelope. What is the expected number of letters that end up in their correct envelope?
insight: Write the count as a sum of indicators, one per letter. Linearity of expectation ignores the dependence between them.
redHerring: Computing the full distribution of fixed points (derangement numbers) before taking the mean.
hints: Write the number of correct letters as a sum of 100 simpler random variables.
Let $I_k = 1$ if letter $k$ is correct. What is $E[I_k]$?
Expectation is linear even when the $I_k$ are dependent.
solution:
Let $I_k$ indicate that letter $k$ lands in its own envelope. Letter $k$ is equally likely to be in any of the 100 envelopes, so $E[I_k] = \tfrac1{100}$.

$E\left[\sum I_k\right] = \sum E[I_k] = 100\cdot\tfrac1{100} = 1$. The $I_k$ are dependent, but linearity does not care.
